FOCUSED.title: AI Skill
FOCUSED.subtitle: Focused learning
FOCUSED.body: Awarded through an eligible focused learning experience, such as a workshop, masterclass, seminar, guest speaker session, or similar short-format activity.
FOCUSED.represents: Development of a defined AI competency.

APPLIED.title: AI Applied Skill
APPLIED.subtitle: Applied learning
APPLIED.body: Awarded through an eligible extended practical learning experience, typically lasting two to three days, such as an intensive workshop, bootcamp, hackathon, or challenge.
APPLIED.represents: Hands-on application of a defined AI competency.

ADVANCED.title: AI Advanced Skill
ADVANCED.subtitle: Extended academic learning
ADVANCED.body: Awarded through the successful completion of an eligible semester-long academic course in which the respective AI competency is a defined and assessed learning outcome.
ADVANCED.represents: Extended and formally assessed development of an AI competency.

stamps.important: The three stamp types reflect different learning formats and depths of engagement. They are not a mandatory sequence: a student does not need an AI Skill before earning an AI Applied Skill or an AI Advanced Skill.

home.lead: One permanent record of the AI skills a BTU student has earned and the university has confirmed. It grows with every new stamp, and anyone can check that it is genuine.

how.title: How a passport is built
how.s1d: Take part in a recognised workshop, bootcamp, hackathon or semester course.
how.s2d: The passport office confirms the skill in the university register.
how.s3d: A new version of the same passport is issued automatically, with every earlier stamp kept.
how.s4d: The document fingerprint is written to a blockchain, signed by BTU's issuing key.

home.stampsLead: Each stamp shows how a skill was earned, from a single masterclass to a full semester course.

employers.title: Checking a candidate's passport?
employers.body: Type the code printed on the passport, or scan its QR code. You will see who holds it, which skills BTU confirmed, whether this is the latest version, and proof that BTU issued it. No account, no fee.

trust.title: Why it can be trusted
trust.d1: Each student receives one passport ID that never changes. Name and first issue date are fixed.
trust.d2: Changing a single character in the PDF changes its fingerprint, and verification fails.
trust.d3: Only BTU's published issuing address can record passports. Its identity is listed on this site.

about.title: About the AI Skills Digital Passport
about.lead: Your personalised and verifiable record of the AI competencies you develop at BTU.
about.p1: AI Skill Stamps may be earned through eligible academic courses, workshops, masterclasses, hackathons, intensive programmes, guest speaker sessions and other AI-related learning experiences recognised by BTU.
about.p2: Participation is voluntary. There is no required number or combination of stamps and no predefined pathway. Students choose learning opportunities according to their interests, studies, professional goals and the areas of AI they want to master.
about.p3: As new competencies are recognised, stamps are added to the same passport. Nothing earlier is removed or rewritten, so the passport becomes an individual AI competency profile over time.
about.versionsBody: Every time a stamp is added, BTU issues a new version of the same passport. Each version has its own verification code. Older versions stay verifiable but are marked as superseded, so a reader always knows whether they are looking at the latest one.

faq.q: Do I need to apply for a passport?
faq.a: No. A passport is created automatically when BTU confirms your first AI skill. You will receive an email when it is ready.
Download the PDF from your passport page and send it, or share the verification link. The reader can check it on this site without an account.

faq.q: My name is misspelled. What now?
faq.a: Names are fixed when the passport is first issued, to protect its integrity. Contact the passport office; corrections are made by staff and recorded in the audit log.

faq.q: What exactly is stored on the blockchain?
faq.a: Only fingerprints: the SHA-256 hash of the PDF, a hash of the verification code, the version number and a hash of the passport ID. No names or personal data are written on chain.
Only if it was recorded in error. Removal requires approval by the passport office and creates a new version; the earlier version is kept for the record.

verify.title: Verify a passport
verify.lead: Enter the 12-character verification code printed on the passport cover. Letters and digits only; dashes are optional.
verify.checking: Checking the record and the blockchain…
verify.invalidFormat: A verification code has 12 characters, for example 7KQ2-M9XD-4TRB.
verify.rateLimited: Too many checks from this network. Please wait a minute and try again.

valid_latest.title: Authentic. This is the latest version.
valid_latest.body: BTU issued this passport version and its record on the blockchain matches.

valid_superseded.title: Authentic, but a newer version exists.
valid_superseded.body: BTU issued this version. The holder has since received an updated passport; ask them for version {latest}.

revoked.title: Revoked by BTU.
revoked.body: This version was withdrawn by the issuer and should not be relied on.

invalid.title: Verification failed.
invalid.body: The record does not match the blockchain or the issuer could not be confirmed. Treat this document as not genuine.

not_found.title: No passport has this code.
not_found.body: Check the code for typos. If it is correct, the document was not issued by BTU.

pending.title: Issued, waiting for blockchain confirmation.
pending.body: This version was created moments ago. Please check again in a minute.

chain_unavailable.title: Blockchain temporarily unreachable.
chain_unavailable.body: The university record exists, but the independent blockchain check could not be completed right now. Try again shortly.

verify.noStamps: No skills listed in this version.

checks.record_on_chain: Version is recorded on the blockchain
checks.document_hash_matches: Document fingerprint matches the issued PDF
checks.code_hash_matches: Verification code matches the on-chain record
checks.issuer_authorised_by_contract: Recorded by an address the registry authorises
checks.issuer_published_by_btu: That address is published by BTU as its issuer

file.title: Check the PDF file itself
file.body: Drop the PDF you received. Its fingerprint is calculated in your browser and compared with the one on the blockchain. The file is never uploaded.
file.match: Exact match. This file is the document BTU issued, unchanged.
file.mismatch: No match. This file differs from the issued document, even if it looks the same. It may have been edited.
file.otherVersion: This file is a genuine BTU passport, but a different version ({version}) from the code you entered.
file.unknown: This file does not match any passport issued by BTU.

byFile.title: No code? Check by file
byFile.body: Drop the passport PDF and we will look up its fingerprint directly.

verify.how1: The code is looked up in BTU's passport register.
verify.how2: The matching record is read from the public blockchain registry.
verify.how3: The document fingerprint and the issuing address are compared with what BTU has published.

issuer.title: Issuer identity
issuer.lead: How to confirm that a passport was issued by Business and Technology University and by no one else.
issuer.name: Issuer
issuer.notDeployed: The registry contract is not deployed yet.
steps: Download the passport PDF and compute its SHA-256 fingerprint (for example: sha256sum passport.pdf).
Read the version record from the registry contract shown above with getVersion(passportIdHash, version), or look the fingerprint up with lookupPdf(sha256).
Check that the stored pdfHash equals your fingerprint and that revokedAt is zero.
Check that the issuer address in the record is one of the authorised addresses listed here and in /.well-known/btu-issuer.json on the BTU domain.
issuer.signatureBody: Each PDF also carries an EIP-712 signature by the issuing key in its document properties (Keywords). Recovering the signer and comparing it with the addresses above confirms the issuer even offline.

sections.p: The BTU AI Skills Digital Passport service (the "Service") is operated by Business and Technology University, 82 I. Chavchavadze Ave, Tbilisi, Georgia ("BTU"). It issues, stores and verifies digital passports that record AI skills confirmed by BTU.
Anyone may use the public verification pages without registering. The personal passport area is available only to BTU students and staff who sign in with a university email address.

A passport certifies that BTU confirmed the listed skills on the listed dates through the listed learning activities. It is not a degree, diploma or transcript and does not replace official academic records.
Passports are updated by issuing new versions under the same passport ID. BTU may revoke a version issued in error. Revoked and superseded versions remain visible as such on the verification page.

You must not alter passport documents, present an altered or revoked passport as valid, attempt to access another person's passport, overload the Service, or try to bypass rate limits or security controls. Automated bulk verification requires prior written agreement with BTU.
Sign-in links are personal and expire after 15 minutes. Do not forward them. Tell the passport office immediately if you believe someone accessed your passport without permission.

Fingerprints of issued documents are written to a public blockchain and cannot be deleted from it. These records contain no personal data. BTU does not control the blockchain network and is not responsible for its availability.
BTU aims to keep the Service available but does not guarantee uninterrupted access. To the extent permitted by Georgian law, BTU is not liable for decisions third parties make based on a passport.

BTU may update these terms; the date above shows the latest change. These terms are governed by the laws of Georgia. Questions: passport office, Business and Technology University, (+995 32) 2 195 015.

Business and Technology University (BTU), 82 I. Chavchavadze Ave, Tbilisi 0179, Georgia, is responsible for personal data processed by the Passport service, in line with the Law of Georgia on Personal Data Protection.

Student number; first and last name in English and Georgian; BTU email address; study programme; the AI skills you earned, with dates, descriptions and the activity through which they were earned; your consent status; sign-in records.

To issue and update your passport, to let you view and download it, and to let third parties you share it with verify it. The legal basis is your consent, given in the passport register, and BTU's legitimate interest in certifying learning outcomes.
Anyone who has your verification code or PDF can see your name, passport ID, the skills listed in that version and their dates. They do not see your email, student number or programme.

Only cryptographic fingerprints (hashes) and version numbers. No name, email or other personal data is written on chain. Because blockchain records cannot be erased, we never place personal data there.
When you check a PDF on the verification page, its fingerprint is calculated in your browser. The file itself is never sent to our servers.

Passport records are kept while you are a student and for 10 years after graduation so that employers can keep verifying them, unless you ask us to close your passport earlier. Sign-in links are deleted within a day of expiry. Verification logs keep only a one-way hash of the visitor's IP address.

You may request access to, correction of, or deletion of your data, and withdraw consent for future updates, by contacting the passport office. Withdrawing consent stops new versions; existing on-chain fingerprints cannot be removed but reveal nothing about you.

Access to personal passports requires a one-time link sent to your university email. Staff actions are restricted by role and recorded in an append-only audit log. Connections are encrypted in production.
We use only strictly necessary cookies: a session cookie after you sign in, a security (CSRF) cookie and a language preference. No advertising or tracking cookies.
